title: Employer Benefit Charging: Determinations Granting Relief on a Separation Response
content:
When the determination on an employer's separation response grants relief, the position is relieved and a relief credit is posted for the determination. This applies to every Employer Benefit Charging position on which the determination of the employer's response grants relief.

The relief credit of a determination on a separation response is not fixed until the position carries the employer's separation response, with the separation reason it reports and the date it was received recorded on it.

Equivalently: so long as the position does not carry the employer's separation response, with its reported separation reason and its date received, the relief credit of the determination is not fixed.

---

**Tool:** `determine_charge_relief_e2b9af19`

**Capability.** Records the determination on an employer's separation response that grants the employer relief from benefit charges, and books the relief credit it carries. One call moves the employer's chargeable position from responded to relieved with the relief basis given, and posts one credit with credit reason `relief_granted`, dated today and counted in today's calendar quarter, against the single posted benefit charge named, for the dollar amount given; the position's total charged falls by that amount. The employer sees the position as relieved and the credit on its next statement.

**Invocation.** Agent-side: the agent unlocks `determine_charge_relief_e2b9af19`, then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Name | Meaning | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `charge_position_id` | The chargeable position whose separation response is determined, as returned by the charge position lookup | Id |
| `customer_id` | The employer's customer reference number that owns the position, as returned by the customer profile lookup | Id |
| `source_charge_id` | The posted benefit charge the relief credit reduces, as returned by the charge ledger lookup | Id |
| `relief_basis` | The ground on which relief is granted | `none` (no relief; not used for a grant), `voluntary_quit_without_good_cause` (the claimant left this employer voluntarily without good cause attributable to it), `discharge_misconduct` (this employer discharged the claimant for misconduct connected with the work), `refused_suitable_work` (the claimant refused suitable work this employer offered), `continuing_part_time` (this employer still employs the claimant part time as in the base period), `agency_error` (the benefits were paid in error by the agency), `not_base_period_employer` (this employer paid no base-period wages or the wages charged to it are wrong), `appeal_decision` (an appeal decision relieved the employer; not used for a determination on a response) |
| `relief_credit_amount` | The dollar amount of the relief credit booked against the named charge | US dollars, 2 decimal places, a plain positive number without a currency sign |

**Return.** `credit_reference` (reference number of the relief credit just posted), `charge_position_id` (the position determined), `source_charge_id` (the posted charge credited), `relief_basis` (the basis recorded), `relief_credit_amount` (dollars credited, 2 decimal places), `credit_quarter` (YYYY-Qn, the calendar quarter in which the credit is posted), `total_charged_after` (the position's total charged once the credit is booked, 2 decimal places), `position_status` (always `relieved` once determined). A receipt carrying a `credit_reference` means relief was granted and the credit posted.
